reason: The mechanism holds up, but as an unconditional 4.5-agent-hour plan item it fails the value lens. VERIFIED: in the exp56 notebook the ILP runs inside the GPU shards (cell 4 l.540-567), and repair runs sequentially over sorted geffs only after the shards merge (cell 5 l.2071-2139). The deadline is checked when each dataset starts and is sticky; _deadline_degrade flips module globals, so each worker would need its own copy, which the design gives it. Exceptions fall back silently to fallback_output_graph. Cell 5 has no global RNG, and its frame, DeepCenter and density caches are per dataset, so a byte-identical CSV is plausible, and the sha256 gate is the right test. Public gain is 0 by construction. VALUE PROBLEM: the private increment over C01 (REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=34200) exists only if the F1 build's full hidden runtime exceeds ~9.5 h. Evidence already in the repo bounds that runtime well below the critic's sim worlds. exp51 has the same GPU phase as x138 (DIFF.md s.2: same D4 TTA, dual seed, edge TTA), a heavier CPU tail (DivNet veto plus ungated DaughterNet, no guard; dummy kernel 1,713 s vs exp56 1,138 s), and it scored within <=7.5 h of submit (submitted 17:09 UTC 24 Sep, score read 00:39 UTC; CONTEXT.md l.1446/1495). exp49 scored within <=7.2 h. Latency >= runtime, and that runtime was measured at the REAL hidden N and density, so the free parameter rho in the sim is already priced in. The sim's N=160-180 / rho 1.6 worlds, where C01 still degrades 19-35%, need G alone ~6.5-7.1 h (141 s/clip on 2 shards). That leaves <1 h for exp51's repair, which costs >=90 s/clip on the dummies, so those worlds are inconsistent with the scored latencies. x138 total is at most about exp51's (no DivNet/DaughterNet, plus flow relink/readmit/gapfill); exp57b is about x138 + DaughterNet, i.e. ~exp51 +/- 0.5 h. Both land well under C01's 9.5 h. P(C01-only F1 still degrades) is ~0.03-0.05 (guess), not 0.1-0.2, so E[private gain over C01] is ~+0.0002-0.0004. That cannot be observed on the LB and is below any decision threshold, while it costs 4.5 agent-hours on 25-26 Sep (competing with C05/C04) plus 2 dummy runs. It also adds a NEW catastrophic-failure mode the idea does not list: K workers with 48-frame caches, DeepCenter and DaughterNet can trigger the Linux OOM killer, which usually picks the largest process, the Jupyter parent holding the merged predictions, not a worker. The kernel then dies and the final gets a scoring error. The 4-clip dummy cannot show hidden-scale RAM. The fail-soft divinsert wrapper is sound, cheap and worth keeping. Its value is also small: exp48/exp51 ran DaughterNet insertion with NO fallback on the whole hidden set and scored, so the insertion code did not raise on hidden data in that stack. Schedule is feasible (see critical_path). Tonight's #34/#35 latencies decide the question for free, which is what step 0 already concedes.
fix_if_any: Split the idea. (A) DO NOW, about 30-40 min of agent time, riding the C01 rider on the F1 build. (1) --set REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=34200. (2) Gate the divinsert block with `and not _deadline_degraded`, so the ungated ~66 s/clip DaughterNet stops after the deadline. (3) Wrap the divinsert block in try/except: keep the input edges, set divins_failed=1, print 'DIVINS FAILED'. Add a test knob BIOHUB_DIVINS_FORCE_FAIL, checked by a local mock test plus one dummy run. The dummy CSV must equal exp56's with FORCE_FAIL=1 and exp57b's with it off. Wrap C04/C05 the same way if they ship. (4) STEP 0, zero slots: the local session timestamps when #34/#35 scores appear (poll the submissions list every 15-20 min from 15:30 UTC, because the CLI shows only submit time) and downloads the exp48/49/51/56/57b logs. The agent computes runtime upper bounds per candidate. (B) BUILD --patch parrepair ONLY IF a trigger fires: latency(#34) >= 7.5 h, or latency(#35) >= 8.5 h, or the step-0 projection of the chosen F1 (incl. any added stage) exceeds ~9 h. If it is built: keep the K=1 default byte-identical path, and have each worker write 1000 to /proc/self/oom_score_adj at start, so the OOM killer takes a worker and not the notebook parent. Size K from RAM measured at repair start (psutil.virtual_memory().available / 5 GB), not a constant. Pass OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 to the workers but compare against a sequential twin also run with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, or drop the thread pin. Give the parent a watchdog that falls back to sequential for unfinished datasets if no worker result arrives within 2x the max dummy repair time. Keep the sha256 gate on the dummy exactly as proposed.
realistic_public_gain: 0 (byte-identical by construction; any public move is LB noise, +/-0.003)
realistic_private_gain: Over C01 alone: ~+0.0002..+0.0004 expected (P(C01-only still degrades) ~0.03-0.05 x ~0.005-0.02 conditional). The existing latencies of exp49/exp51 (<=7.2/7.5 h, same GPU phase, heavier tail) rule out the sim's high-N/dense worlds. The divinsert gate + fail-soft wrapper alone: ~+0 to +0.0005 (insurance). Part B becomes worth ~+0.005..+0.02 only in the triggered world (latency #34 >= 7.5 h), which tonight's scores reveal.
